paper_title: SRPO Enhancing Multimodal LLM Reasoning via Reflection-Aware   Reinforcement Learning
caption: Performance of various RL methods with and without self-reflection.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart illustrates the performance, measured as accuracy in percentage, of various reinforcement learning (RL) methods—with and without self-reflection—across three distinct domains: Mathverse, MMLU, and Physics. The horizontal axis categorizes the three domains, while the vertical axis represents accuracy (%) ranging from 50% to 62%, marked at 2% intervals. Six distinct methods are compared, each represented by a uniquely colored and patterned bar: DAPO+Self-reflection (solid blue), DAPO (blue with diagonal stripes), SRPO (solid orange), GRPO (orange with diagonal stripes), PPO+Self-reflection (solid green), and PPO (green with diagonal stripes), as indicated in the legend. Within each domain, the bars are grouped together, allowing direct comparison between methods. In Mathverse, DAPO+Self-reflection achieves approximately 56%, while SRPO reaches around 55.8%, and PPO+Self-reflection is near 54.5%. In MMLU, DAPO+Self-reflection peaks at roughly 57%, followed closely by SRPO at ~57.2%, with PPO+Self-reflection at ~56.2%. In Physics, DAPO+Self-reflection attains the highest accuracy at ~61%, followed by SRPO at ~60.5%, and PPO+Self-reflection at ~59%. The chart visually suggests that methods incorporating self-reflection (DAPO+Self-reflection, PPO+Self-reflection) generally outperform their non-self-reflection counterparts (DAPO, PPO) across all domains, with SRPO consistently performing competitively. No bars are visually emphasized through shading or highlighting beyond their standard color and pattern coding.
model_annotations.Chinese: This bar chart presents a comparative evaluation of the accuracy (%) achieved by six different reinforcement learning methods—DAPO+Self-reflection, DAPO, GRPO, SRPO, PPO+Self-reflection, and PPO—across three distinct multimodal reasoning benchmarks: Mathverse, MMLU, and Physics. The horizontal axis categorizes the three benchmarks, while the vertical axis quantifies accuracy on a linear scale ranging from 50% to 62%, with major gridlines and tick marks at 2% intervals (50, 52, 54, 56, 58, 60, 62). Each benchmark group contains six adjacent bars, color- and pattern-coded according to the legend: solid blue for DAPO+Self-reflection, diagonally striped light blue for DAPO, orange with diagonal stripes for GRPO, solid orange for SRPO, solid green for PPO+Self-reflection, and diagonally striped green for PPO. In the Mathverse category, DAPO+Self-reflection reaches approximately 56.2%, DAPO is at ~53.3%, GRPO at ~53.6%, SRPO at ~55.8%, PPO+Self-reflection at ~54.6%, and PPO at ~53.4%. For MMLU, DAPO+Self-reflection scores ~57.2%, DAPO ~56.0%, GRPO ~55.8%, SRPO ~57.4%, PPO+Self-reflection ~56.2%, and PPO ~54.8%. In the Physics category, DAPO+Self-reflection achieves the highest value at ~61.2%, followed by SRPO at ~60.8%, GRPO at ~58.2%, DAPO at ~57.6%, PPO at ~57.2%, and PPO+Self-reflection at ~59.2%. The bars within each group are arranged in a fixed order as per the legend, with no explicit sorting by value; however, the SRPO method consistently ranks among the top performers across all three benchmarks, particularly excelling in Physics. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, outlines, or annotations beyond their inherent color and pattern coding.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the performance, measured as accuracy in percentage, of various reinforcement learning (RL) methods—both with and without self-reflection—across three multimodal reasoning benchmarks: Mathverse, MMLU, and Physics. The vertical axis represents Accuracy (%) ranging from 50 to 62, with tick marks at 2% intervals. The horizontal axis categorizes the three datasets. Six distinct methods are compared, each represented by a uniquely colored and patterned bar: DAPO+Self-reflection (solid blue), DAPO (hatched blue-gray), SRPO (solid orange), GRPO (hatched orange), PPO+Self-reflection (solid green), and PPO (hatched green), as indicated in the legend. In Mathverse, DAPO+Self-reflection achieves ~56.1%, DAPO ~53.1%, SRPO ~55.8%, GRPO ~53.5%, PPO+Self-reflection ~54.5%, and PPO ~53.3%. In MMLU, DAPO+Self-reflection reaches ~57.0%, DAPO ~55.9%, SRPO ~57.2%, GRPO ~55.8%, PPO+Self-reflection ~56.2%, and PPO ~54.6%. In Physics, DAPO+Self-reflection peaks at ~61.0%, DAPO ~57.6%, SRPO ~60.6%, GRPO ~58.1%, PPO+Self-reflection ~59.1%, and PPO ~57.0%. Across all datasets, DAPO+Self-reflection consistently shows the highest accuracy, followed closely by SRPO, while PPO without self-reflection consistently underperforms. The chart visually emphasizes the performance boost conferred by self-reflection, particularly in Physics, where the gap between self-reflection and non-self-reflection variants is most pronounced.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm vergleicht die Genauigkeit (in Prozent) verschiedener Verstärkungslernmethoden — mit und ohne Selbstreflexion — auf drei multimodalen Reasoning-Benchmarks: Mathverse, MMLU und Physics. Die horizontale Achse listet die drei Aufgabendomänen auf, während die vertikale Achse die Genauigkeit von 50 % bis 62 % in 2 %-Schritten anzeigt. Für jede Domäne sind fünf Methoden dargestellt: DAPO+Self-reflection (blau), DAPO (hellblau gestreift), GRPO (orange gestreift), SRPO (orange) und PPO+Self-reflection (grün), sowie PPO (grün gestreift), wobei letztere in der Legende separat aufgeführt sind. In Mathverse liegt DAPO+Self-reflection bei etwa 56 %, DAPO bei 53 %, GRPO bei 53,5 %, SRPO bei 55,8 % und PPO+Self-reflection bei 54,5 %. In MMLU erreicht DAPO+Self-reflection etwa 57,2 %, DAPO 56 %, GRPO 55,8 %, SRPO 57,5 % und PPO+Self-reflection 56,2 %. In Physics ist DAPO+Self-reflection mit etwa 61,2 % am höchsten, gefolgt von SRPO mit 60,8 %, GRPO mit 58,2 %, DAPO mit 57,5 %, PPO+Self-reflection mit 59,2 % und PPO mit 57,2 %. Die Balken sind in jeder Gruppe nebeneinander angeordnet, ohne Sortierung nach Höhe, und die Farben sowie Muster entsprechen der Legende oben rechts. Die Darstellung zeigt, dass Methoden mit Selbstreflexion (DAPO+Self-reflection, PPO+Self-reflection) in den meisten Fällen höhere Genauigkeiten erzielen als ihre Baseline-Versionen ohne Reflexion, wobei SRPO in zwei von drei Aufgaben die zweithöchste oder höchste Genauigkeit erreicht.
